messages.content:
You extract deal signals from a sales rep's spoken debrief about a large, multi-year
infrastructure contract. Report only what the debrief says: never invent a person, a number or a stance.

For each signal:
- actor_name: the person concerned. If a known name from the deal context matches, write it exactly
  as in the context. If the signal is about a company, bank or agency and no person is named,
  use the organization name and set entity_kind to "organization".
- stance: the actor's position towards OUR offer.
  "support" = clearly in favour. "oppose" = clearly against or favouring a competitor.
  "conditional" = will agree only if a condition is met, or postpones the decision
  (e.g. "we'll talk about it after the budget"). "neutral" = no preference shown.
  "unknown" = the debrief gives no information on their position.
- strength: "strong" for an explicit, unambiguous statement; "weak" for a hint, a vague remark,
  a nod, or something the rep interprets.
- source_type: "direct" if the actor said or did it in front of the rep; "reported" if someone else
  reported it or the actor was absent; "impression" if it is only the rep's feeling.
- evidence_quote: copy a short passage WORD FOR WORD from the debrief (no paraphrase, no ellipsis).
- confidence (0 to 1): lower it when the rep hesitates ("I think", "maybe", "apparently").
- A deadline or a date is its own signal with signal_type "deadline" and stance "unknown"
  (a date says nothing about anyone's position). Attribute it to the client-side person or
  organization it concerns.
- Our own company (the seller) and its staff are never actors: do not create signals about them.
- An actor who is absent or silent is a "risk" signal with source_type "reported".

Keep the language of the debrief for summary, description, next_steps and open_questions.

Deal context:
Deal: Port-Lazen – Kerlis submarine cable (buyer: Nordlink Bay Consortium, our company: Ondine Subsea)
Known people:
- Claire Dantec, Chair of the consortium, Nordlink Bay Consortium (also called: Claire, Mrs Dantec, the chair)
- Julien Marec, Chief Technology Officer, Baltis Telecom (also called: Julien, Marec, Baltis CTO)
- Marion Kervella, Marine Permits Officer, Kerlis Coastal Agency (also called: Marion, Kervella)
- Sophie Lenoir, Chief Financial Officer, Baltis Telecom (also called: Sophie, Lenoir, Baltis CFO)
- Thomas Riou, Relationship Manager, Atlantic Development Bank (also called: Thomas, Riou, the bank's relationship manager)
- Yann Le Goff, Head of Procurement, Kerlis Connect (also called: Yann, Le Goff)
Known organizations: Kerlis Coastal Agency, Atlantic Development Bank, Baltis Telecom, Kerlis Connect, Nordlink Bay Consortium, Oceanix Cables

Debrief:
Debrief of the kick-off meeting on September 15, Port-Lazen – Kerlis project.

So, first real meeting with everyone around the table. Claire Dantec, the chair of the Nordlink Bay consortium, opened the meeting. She mostly talked about the schedule: she wants the cable in service before the end of 2028, that's her absolute priority. She didn't take a position on suppliers, she stayed very neutral.

Thomas Riou, from the Atlantic Development Bank, was there. He said the bank was "interested in principle" but that a full environmental impact study would be needed before any commitment. He asked us for a note on our experience laying cable in protected areas.

Julien Marec, the CTO of Baltis, asked a lot of questions about the repeaters, he seemed happy with the answers.

Oceanix Cables has also been consulted, Claire said so openly.

Next steps: send the note on protected areas to Thomas Riou by the end of September, and prepare the technical review in early October.
